_comment: Permission policy for edullm-reservoir-ingest — WHAT this role may touch.
Least privilege for §5.6 phase 0 (HF ingest) + §9.7 item 4 (the synthetic id partition). The
job reads upstream documents from Hugging Face over HTTPS and writes derived artifacts to one
landing prefix. It is a BUILD role, not a publishing role.
THE POINT OF A SEPARATE ROLE. The validator role is the only principal that can write
s3://edullm-data — that is the airlock. Running a 5 TB bulk-download job under it would put a
program doing wide-open network fetches in possession of the one key to the published bucket,
so a bug in ingest becomes a bug that can write published data. This role simply is not
granted that, and since 2026-07-31 the bucket policy (edullm-data-airlock-v2) also denies it
explicitly, so an accidental widening of THIS file still cannot reach the published bucket.
NO s3:DeleteObject ANYWHERE, including its own staging prefix. A failed attempt uses a fresh
run id and the `expire-ingest-30d` lifecycle rule reclaims the partial prefix. Same reasoning
as the prm800k role: a retry that can delete is a retry that can destroy a different run's
evidence while you are trying to work out what went wrong.
NO s3:PutObject on any *manifest.json*. `edullm-landing-manifest-created` matches that key
SUFFIX with no prefix constraint, so writing one anywhere in landing fires the validator
against a build artifact. `ingest_reservoir._assert_safe_key` already refuses the name in
code; this is the same rule enforced where code cannot be edited around. Belt and braces on
purpose — the code guard protects against a typo, the IAM guard against a different program.
Deploy with the infra-deployer role:
aws iam create-role --role-name edullm-reservoir-ingest \
--assume-role-policy-document file://infra/08-reservoir-ingest-trust-policy.json
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name edullm-reservoir-ingest \
--policy-name reservoir-ingest --policy-document file://infra/08-reservoir-ingest-policy.json
Then SMOKE-TEST the deny, do not simulate it: iam:simulate-principal-policy is documented in
CLAUDE.md as returning false denials for this account (11 known). Submit a job that attempts a
PutObject to edullm-data and read the error.
s3:GetLifecycleConfiguration IS REQUIRED, and its absence cost the first live run. The job's
own start-up guard reads the bucket's lifecycle rules to refuse staging terabytes under a
prefix nothing will expire. Least privilege means granting what the code actually calls, and a
read of a bucket's expiry rules leaks nothing. It is bucket-scoped, not `*`.
The general lesson: a guard is code, and code needs permissions. Writing a safety check and
then not granting it is how a safety check becomes an outage.
